bib.title: Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Overview (Chapter 5: Multi-agent RL)

question: What are the game formalisms, solution concepts and algorithms of multi-agent RL?
contributions: Brief MARL introduction based on Albrecht, Christianos and Schafer (ACS24): games, solution concepts, algorithms, and a pointer to MARL for LLM agents.

limits: Brief introduction that follows [ACS24]; most algorithm results are cited, not measured here.
MMDS belief-state and learned-world-model errors are open questions (Sec 5.3.11.4).
MARL for LLM agents gets only a three-sentence pointer (Sec 5.3.12); no RAG content.
Policy Gradient Hypothesis of Rudolph et al. is stated as a hypothesis, tested only on small imperfect-information games.
No numbers for MMDS results in the text; only qualitative 'modest gains'.
practices: Treat other agents as part of the environment and use single-agent RL (independent learning, IQL, IPPO) as the simplest baseline; it may not converge since policy-gradient learning of multiple agents can cycle (Sec 5.3.2).
Use centralized training with decentralized execution: centralized critics are valid as long as actors use only local information at execution (MAPPO) (Sec 5.3.3).
In common-reward games use value decomposition (VDN sum, QMIX monotone mixing) that satisfies the IGM property (Sec 5.3.4).
Self-play converges to Nash only for perfect-information zero-sum games; otherwise it can cycle and be exploitable, so use population training (PSRO) or best-response methods (Sec 5.3.5, 5.3.8).
Measure two-player zero-sum policies by exploitability and general policies by NashConv (Sec 5.2.3, 5.2.5).
Tune the entropy penalty much higher for two-player zero-sum PPO (0.05-2.0) before concluding policy gradient is inferior (Sec 5.3.10.2).
Use Shapley values to address multi-agent credit assignment in cooperative games, including token importance in prompts (Sec 5.2.12).
Use Stackelberg (leader/follower) for setter-solver curriculum problems; solved by backward induction (Sec 5.2.13).

terms.definition: a single interaction between n >= 2 agents, each with finite actions and a reward function
a multi-agent version of an MDP
Partially Observed Stochastic Game, a multi-agent version of a POMDP
special case with the same reward for all agents, so only cooperative behaviour
Factored Observation Stochastic Game: POSG with observations split into public and private
policy maximizing agent i's expected return against fixed policies of the others
no agent can improve its expected return by changing its own policy while others stay fixed
half the sum of each player's best-response gain against the other's policy in 2p0s games; zero at a Nash equilibrium
sum over agents of the incentive to deviate to a best response
Nash-like equilibrium where best responses are soft, entropy-regularized policies
central policy over joint actions from which no agent gains by deviating after receiving its recommendation
no other joint policy improves one agent without lowering another
individual global max: local argmax actions are jointly globally optimal
policy space response oracle: population-based training that solves a meta-game over policy sets and adds oracle best responses
counterfactual regret minimization, regret matching on counterfactual values for imperfect-information 2p0s games
magnetic mirror descent: policy gradient with magnet-policy KL and proximal KL terms, converging to QRE
MMD search: decision-time planning using MMD as the local policy update
